title: Derivative-closed factorial seminorm versus quartic source-history growth
question: Can a factorial-weighted coefficient seminorm, which closes the source derivative at fixed radius, also control repeated insertion of the actual quartic Q3 source top monomial in both source orientations at a fixed positive final radius?

model.factorial_seminorm: For f(a)=sum_n c_n a^n, ||f||_(S,!)=sum_n |c_n| n! S^n.
model.derivative_closure: ||D_a f||_(S,!) = S^(-1)||f||_(S,!) on finite polynomials, so this candidate closes the source derivative without radius loss.
model.actual_source_slice: The registered center and reverse Q3 source polynomials both have coefficient -51/140 on the pure a^4 monomial at q=v=0.
model.top_monomial_operator: T=(51/140) a^4 D_a is the positive absolute-value top-monomial branch of the source insertion envelope.
model.norm_ratio: At input radius S and output radius S', the witness ratio is (51/140)^m prod_j(1+3j) (1+3m)! S'^(1+3m)/S.
model.orientation: The pure a^4 coefficient has the same absolute value for the center and reverse source orientation.

scope.not_closed: This rejects only the positive top-monomial envelope in this factorial coefficient topology. It does not exclude cancellations in the complete Q3 commutator, a different non-Leibniz or state-weighted topology, an actual common core, QFT reconstruction, the gap, the continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

adversarial_review.check: The factorial weight is differentiated algebraically; the factor m exactly cancels the ratio m!/(m-1)! and gives the stated S^(-1) bound.
The pure a^4 coefficient is rederived from the registered center and reverse source polynomials, not inserted as a fitted constant.
T is the positive absolute-value top branch of a coefficient majorant; no equality with the signed full Q3 history is claimed.
The exact m=8 witness is evaluated at S=1/4 and S'=1/8; the factorial lower bound shows every fixed positive radius ratio is eventually dominated, while the finite row remains the declared fixture.
Center and reverse top coefficients agree and the 12-branch comparison is retained only as a finite history baseline.
Lean R290 checks the rational derivative identity, exact m=8 witness and factorial lower-bound fixture; it does not formalize Q3 domains or limits.
No common dynamics, KMS/OS, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A conclusion is inferred.

qft_interface.closed: A derivative-closed factorial coefficient seminorm is algebraically compatible with D_a, but its actual quartic top-source insertion branch has a superexponential repeated-history witness in both orientations.
qft_interface.open: A cancellation-aware actual Q3 common-core or state-weighted estimate, factorial spatial incidence, first passage, exhaustion, common alpha, Hamiltonian/KMS identification, OS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: No heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner is supplied by this route boundary.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing route boundary. The factorial seminorm closes the formal derivative but the positive top-monomial quartic insertion envelope is not exponentially bounded at any fixed positive final radius. This is not a no-go theorem for the signed Q3 dynamics or QFT.
next_action: Retain the factorial topology only if an actual Q3 cancellation or state-weighted estimate removes the top-monomial branch; otherwise test a genuinely different common-core construction before common-alpha promotion.
